# cancho-gpu

> A compiler for typed tile kernels (the .chx language), written in cancho: it checks a typed tile program (linearity, bounds, shapes, the threadgroup budget) and lowers it to CUDA C and Metal, recorded as goldens for 433 cases (403 emit, 30 refused); those cases first agreed byte for byte with an independent Rust implementation, which was the test oracle until it was retired, and what the kernels compute is held to float64 references for every numeric kernel family. It links only libc; its authority report names what it may do (args, stderr, file read and write, heap, stdout) and no network or foreign code. Alpha: the compiler, device path, model-reading core (GGUF, safetensors, BPE tokenizer, sampler) and the decode kernels of an attention layer are built; it runs Qwen2.5-0.5B and Qwen3.8-27B on a Metal GPU and serves the 27B over an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. A kernel can be run on inputs you give it (`cancho-gpu run`, CPU interpreter only). Models are also trained on a Metal GPU in sessions (docs/resident.md): a small network with Adam, a GPT of up to 59.95 M parameters (trained and served), a 0.85 M-parameter ResNet (87.4% on real CIFAR-10, no augmentation), and Qwen2.5-0.5B and 1.5B fine-tuned with LoRA (and the 0.5B with every parameter), with gradients and loss curves held to transformers, peft and torch. Limits: one machine (Apple M4 Max), one run and one seed each, CUDA run on one NVIDIA L4 only (compiles, 176 of 188 cases agree with the interpreter), no tuned model for the cancho-code experiment (M8) yet, a 4-bit NVFP4 base is built for the 1.5B's LoRA (docs/resident.md section 27) but the 7B has not been run.

## Use it
- [Quick start](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu#quick-start): build the compiler at the pinned revision, emit a kernel.
- Commands: `cancho-gpu emit <file.chx> <dir> [name=value ...] [--run]`, `cancho-gpu check <file.chx> [name=value ...] [--run]`, `cancho-gpu run <file.chx> [name=value ...] [--target T] [--in NAME FILE ...] [--out NAME ...]`, `cancho-gpu gguf <file.gguf> [--sum]`, `cancho-gpu safetensors <file>`, `cancho-gpu tokenize <tokenizer.json|model.gguf> <corpus>`, `cancho-gpu sample <logits.f32> <vocab> <temperature> <top_p> <top_k> <seed>`. A refusal is `error[<rule>]: <message>` on stderr, exit 1; a usage mistake is exit 2.

## Facts that matter when calling it
- Targets: nvidia-ada (CUDA C) and apple-m-series (Metal), each from the file's schedule. amd-cdna3 is a schedule row with no emitter.
- Device paths: Metal has run on Apple Silicon (numerical agreement, and speed for the runners and training sessions: docs/benchmark.md, docs/resident.md). CUDA is verified against a mock driver only; no real NVIDIA GPU run yet.
- `gguf` reads the first 32 MiB of a file: metadata and tensor directory, never tensor values. It refuses hostile input with a rule tag (gguf-truncated, gguf-version, gguf-duplicate, ...).
- Kernels: rope, kv_append, attention (head dimension 256; at most 1364 positions on Metal) and attn_gate in tests/chx/. Split-KV attention for longer contexts cannot be written in the surface yet.
- Model runner: `cancho-gpu-run <model dir> tests/chx "<prompt>" <new tokens>` for Qwen2-architecture bf16 checkpoints (256-position context, no chat template), 6 to 12 ms a token. Qwen3.8-27B: `cancho-gpu-run35 <ollama store> tests/chx "<prompt>" <new tokens>` runs `qwen3.8:27b-mlx` (NVFP4, 48 gated-delta layers) at 27.4 tokens a second (39.9 with speculative decoding by the model's own draft head; Ollama 45.3 in the same benchmark run, docs/benchmark.md), matching a reference's golden log-probabilities to 1e-4 (1024-position context).
- Serving: `cancho-gpu-serve <ollama store> tests/chx --port 8080 [--api-key K]` is an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` (streaming, the model's chat template held to jinja2, thinking mode) over Qwen3.8-27B, one request at a time, 1024-position context (docs/serving.md).
- Running a kernel on your own numbers: `cancho-gpu run` reads each read-only parameter from a text file (`--in NAME FILE`, whitespace-separated, exactly the parameter's size, at most 16 MiB, none optional) and prints a writable one whole (`--out NAME`) from the CPU interpreter; `--target` is required when the file has both schedules. Backward kernels `bwd_dx`, `bwd_dw`, `bwd_db` and `bwd_sigmoid` are in tests/chx/. A least-squares fit driven by cancho-opt's BFGS with these kernels as the objective converges in 12 evaluations at 28 to 36 ms each.
- Training sessions (docs/resident.md): `cancho-gpu-metal-session` keeps parameters, optimiser state and data on the GPU; directives `resident`, `table`, `carry`, `steps`, `alias`, `save` and the request `checkpoint`; a resident or table file may be binary (`f32`, `f16`; `i8` for a resident 4-bit base; no 16 MiB cap; a text file is capped). The surface has `relu`, `step`, `tanh`, `mma`, `mma_nn` and `mma_tn`; it has no atomics, no index-valued load and no `max a b`.
- Measured against torch on MPS (one machine, one run each; docs/resident.md sections 12 to 24, summarised in the README table): faster per step for the GPT (59.95 M parameters: 167.8 ms against 196.7), for Qwen2.5 LoRA (0.5B: 889.2 ms against 1,142.0 with float16 autocast; 1.5B: 2,467.3 against 2,743.8) and for 0.5B full fine-tuning (1,381.4 against 1,450.8); slower on the CNN (17.6 ms against 10.6) and, when decoding, than Ollama (27B: 39.9 with speculation against 45.3) and MLX-LM (0.5B: 180.4 against 347.2 tokens a second).
- Batched decode and an on-device sampler: docs/decode.md, docs/sampler.md (same 48 tokens as transformers, 35.6 ms a step at 32 x 1,152). A complete optimiser: docs/optimizer.md. QLoRA on a 4-bit base: 1.5B and 7B (docs/resident.md sections 27 and 28; the 7B ran 90 steps, held-out loss 2.1026 to 1.7556).
- Images: text to image with Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo at 1024 x 1024 in about 52 s against torch MPS's 41 s (estimated), the image 49.3 dB from float64 against torch's 26.2 dB; and photo editing end to end on the GPU (vision tower, text encoder reading the photograph, VAE encoder, transformer with a cached prefix, decoder): one real photograph in 92 s against torch's 54 s (torch's is warm, its 17 s load not counted; ours loads 30 GB of weights; about 70 s if everything were loaded, estimated; docs/diffusion.md D11), the same edit (docs/diffusion.md D9; a session request `reload` keeps the weights on the device between steps, docs/resident.md section 29; the stages share one process, the softmax statistics take one pass over the scores and the stages' results leave as binary files, D9k, D10 and D12; requests `reload` and `copy`, docs/resident.md sections 29 and 30). Weight-space editing, with negative results: docs/weight-space-w4.md.
- Compared with OpenNN: docs/comparison.md is a forward pass on a CPU only, small, with no ratio claimed; no GPU comparison with OpenNN exists, and the one training comparison (docs/resident.md sections 13 and 14) is against its CPU path.
- Not implemented or not shown: concurrent requests, tools, video, AMD, Hopper, CUDA on hardware, contexts above 128 (GPT training) or 512 (Qwen training) or 1024 (decode runners), CIFAR-10 at 90% (87.4% reached), a 7B-model result beyond one 90-step QLoRA run with no gradient check, tuned-model results for the cancho-code experiment, GPU timing of the ResNet-18 vision backbone. See "Known gaps" in the README.

## Optional
- [Design](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/design.md): how the compiler is built and every difference from the Rust.
- [Device](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/device.md): driving a GPU, and what stays unproven.
- [Runtime](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/runtime.md): the GGUF and safetensors readers, the tokenizer and the sampler.
- [Inference](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/inference.md): running Qwen2.5-0.5B on a Metal GPU.
- [Qwen3.8-27B](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/qwen35.md): the 27B runner, its kernels and how it is checked.
- [Kernels](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/kernels.md): the attention-layer decode kernels and the context limit.
- [Run](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/run.md): a kernel on your own inputs, with its gates and numbers.
- [Compared with OpenNN](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/comparison.md): a forward pass measured on a CPU, with the differences and where cancho-gpu is worse.
- [Training](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/training.md): whether training belongs here, and what the surface can express of a backward pass.
- [Sessions and models](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/resident.md): training on the device (Adam, GPT, CNN, Qwen2.5 forward, LoRA and full fine-tuning, a ResNet-18-class backbone), with every number and its conditions.
- [Roadmap of models](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/roadmap-models.md): the milestones M1 to M9 (M8: fine-tuning for cancho-code, design and baselines; M9: vision for cancho-robot) and the gaps in the language.
- [Benchmark](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/benchmark.md): decode speed against Ollama, MLX-LM and transformers.
- [Issues](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/issues): the open slices.
